title: Lock your accounts, use Wi-Fi safely and guard your privacy

say: Lock your accounts, use Wi-Fi safely, and guard your privacy.
This is the video for module three: protecting your accounts, connection and privacy.
Criminals do not guess passwords one by one. Programs try millions of common passwords, and lists leaked from hacked websites.
So a name and birth year, or the same password everywhere, is easy to break.
Instead, pick four random words that do not belong together, and join them with a number or symbol. For example, Mango, Bicycle, Rain, Okra, 7.
Use a different one for each important account, and let Google Password Manager remember them for you.
For example, Yetunde in Lagos used one password on four sites. A recipe website was hacked, and then Gmail warned her about a sign-in attempt from another country.

say: Two-step verification means signing in needs something you know, your password, and something you have, your phone. Start with email. Open myaccount dot google dot com, tap Security, then 2-Step Verification.

panel.heading: Turn on two-step verification
items: Google: Security, then 2-Step Verification
Add Google prompts and a second method
Write backup codes on paper, keep them at home
WhatsApp: Account, Two-step verification, 6-digit PIN

say: Add Google prompts, and a second method such as an authenticator app. SMS codes are better than nothing, but weaker.

say: In WhatsApp, open Settings, Account, Two-step verification, and create a 6-digit PIN that is not your birthday or bank PIN.

say: Watch for the wrong code trick. A friend's number says, I sent you a code by mistake, please send it back. That code is your own WhatsApp code. Sending it hands over your account.

panel.rule: Never share any code that arrives on your phone.

say: Patience in Benin City typed her Gmail password into a fake login page by mistake. But she had turned on 2-Step Verification a month earlier.

items: She typed her password into a fake page
Her phone asked: Is it you trying to sign in?
She tapped No. Google blocked it
She changed her password straight away

say: Anyone can create a Wi-Fi network with a trusted name. Zainab in Kano saw two eatery networks with almost the same name. She asked the cashier which was real.

panel.heading: Safe habits on free Wi-Fi
items: Ask staff for the exact network name
Never type passwords on a Wi-Fi sign-in page
Banking and transfers on mobile data only
When you leave, tap the network and Forget

say: A real sign-in page asks only for a code, phone number or room number. Never your email or bank password.

panel.heading: Safe habits on free Wi-Fi
items: Ask staff for the exact network name
Never type passwords on a Wi-Fi sign-in page
Banking and transfers on mobile data only
When you leave, tap the network and Forget

say: Zainab used the Wi-Fi to download a course video. But to check that her client's 45,000 naira had arrived, she turned Wi-Fi off and opened her bank app on mobile data.

panel.heading: Safe habits on free Wi-Fi
items: Ask staff for the exact network name
Never type passwords on a Wi-Fi sign-in page
Banking and transfers on mobile data only
When you leave, tap the network and Forget
panel.rule: Banking and passwords: switch to mobile data.

say: When she left, she chose Forget, so her phone would not join again by itself. At home, protect your own hotspot with WPA2 or WPA3 and a long password.

say: Criminals use your details to build believable scams. So once a month, check these. A torch app does not need your contacts, so remove permissions an app does not need.
Aisha in Abuja set WhatsApp groups to My contacts and silenced unknown callers. The scam group invitations and night calls stopped.

panel.heading: Your monthly privacy check
items: App permissions reviewed
Google Privacy Checkup done
WhatsApp set to My contacts
Silence unknown callers on
Facebook posts set to Friends
Find My Device on

say: Never post ID slips or cards. A fraudster who sees your child's school uniform can pretend to be a teacher calling about an emergency.

panel.heading: Keep these off public pages
left: BVN or NIN slip, ATM card

say: Privacy is not hiding. It is choosing. Ask yourself, would I be comfortable if a stranger who wanted to cheat me saw this?

panel.heading: Keep these off public pages
left: BVN or NIN slip, ATM card

say: To remember. Use four random words, different for each account. Turn on two-step verification, starting with email. Never share a code.
Keep money and passwords off public Wi-Fi. And remove app permissions an app does not need.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Four random words, different for each account
Turn on two-step verification, email first
Never share any code sent to your phone
Money and passwords: mobile data, not public Wi-Fi
Remove permissions apps do not need

say: Now practise. Change your email password, run Password Checkup, turn on two-step verification for Google and WhatsApp, forget old public networks, and tune your privacy settings.
